properties.IncidentOverview: A storm moved through northern Harney County on July 22; 2026; yielding hundreds of positive lightning strikes. The Bald Mountain Fire was discovered on the afternoon of July 23; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone; Rangeland Fire Protection Association and the Egypt Fire responded promptly but were unable to contain the fast moving wildfire. Southern Area Team 2 is responsible for management of the fire; along with the Stubble; Crater; Second Flats and Jackass Butte fires. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

A lightning storm moved through Eastern Oregon on July 15; 2026; igniting multiple fires. The Egypt Fire was discovered on the morning of July 16; 2026. Initial attack resources from the Burns Interagency Fire Zone responded promptly but were spread thin due to several other starts in the area. Southern Area Team 2 took command of the Egypt Fire on July 19 at 6 AM. Priorities remain public and firefighter safety; private lands; and critical infrastructure. Firefighters are working the fire as directly as possible to protect these values at risk; using both ground resources and multiple helicopters and fixed wing aircraft.

U.S. Wildland Fire Service wildland firefighters are responding to the Island Fire; which was reported on July 25 at approximately 9 p.m. The fire is located about 25 miles southwest of Ehrenberg; Arizona; in the Cibola National Wildlife Refuge. The cause of the fire is under investigation. The fire is estimated to be approximately 3;145 acres and is 65% contained. The reduced acreage is due to more accurate mapping. Wildland firefighters are actively working to suppress the fire and protect life; property; and natural and cultural resources. Closures: The Cibola National Wildlife Refuge’s Island Management Unit is closed to the public and Hart Mine Road is closed at the refuge boundary. The bridge on Hart Mine Road crossing the Colorado River collapsed into the river. Pedestrians; motorists; and boaters should avoid the area.

The Castle Fire was first reported on July 22; 2026. It is currently estimated to be 1;727 acres. Hand-crews; engines; water tenders; dozers and a variety of other heavy equipment are on scene; with more requested. Crews continue to work on indirect containment lines. Dozer line was established on the southwestern flank of the fire. Central and Eastern Oregon; as well as other areas of the country have a high number of fires; so resources are limited; and may be responding from a long distance away. California Complex Incident Management has assumed management of the Fire as of 6:00 this morning. This team will be integrated with an International CIMT from Australia. Moderate temperatures have aided in overnight recovery and moderated fire growth in the morning hours. Firefighters are using tactics and strategies that provide the highest likelihood of success while mitigating risks to responders in this steep terrain. Crews and heavy equipment continue to strengthen direct and indirect lines where they can be defended and successfully contain the fire. Area Closures: A portion of the Umpqua National Forest is closed near the Castle Fire (Little Black Rock and Castle Creek areas); as well as South Umpqua Falls Campground and Day Use Area. The purpose of this Order is to protect public and firefighter health and safety during active wildfire suppression operations. Visit the Umpqua Alerts and Notices page at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/castle-fire-closure - You may also click on the Closure Order (pdf) and Closure Order Map (pdf). Public Use Restrictions: As of Friday; July 24; 2026 the Umpqua National Forest moved to Public Use Restrictions (PURs) Stage 2 across the whole Forest. In PURs Stage 2; chttps://fire.airnow.gov/#7/44.73/-117.986ampfires in wilderness and public firewood cutting (with an internal combustion engine) will no longer be allowed. Campfires within Forest Service-constructed concrete or metal fire rings within designated developed recreation sites are exempt. More Information is available at https://www.fs.usda.gov/r06/umpqua/alerts/public-use-restrictions-stage-2 Smoke Impacts: With a significant number of fires burning within Oregon; please take steps to protect yourself from smoke. Smoke can irritate the eyes and lungs and worsen some medical conditions. People most at risk include infants and young children; people with heart or lung disease; older adults and pregnant people. Smoke levels can change rapidly depending on weather. Check current conditions on the U.S. Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program ; the Oregon Smoke Information Blog ; DEQ’s Air Quality Index ; or by downloading the free OregonAIR app on your smartphone. About the Forest: The Umpqua National Forest protects 982;510 acres of forest across Douglas; Lane; and Jackson Counties. High Cascades glaciation; whitewater rapids; and explosive volcanic events have shaped the Forest's spectacular scenery and abundant natural resources. Verdant stands of hemlock; fir and cedar transition to forests of mixed conifers and hardwoods at lower elevations; while alpine ecosystems dominate high peaks like Mount Thielsen. The Forest's waterways and diverse ecosystems create desirable habitat for many species of fish and wildlife; in addition to providing outstanding recreational opportunities to our local communities and visitors.

Current Situation: On Monday; California Interagency Incident Management Team 5 arrived in Vale; Oregon; to take command of the ongoing Hat Fire. We want to take a moment to acknowledge and commend the dedicated firefighters who have been working around the clock; facing challenging conditions to contain and suppress the Hat Fire. Through their efforts; significant progress has been made to successfully hold the fire in its current footprint; with no new growth yesterday. Today; firefighters will continue to monitor and secure the area while improving the existing containment lines. Additional firefighters have arrived to assist in constructing a hand line in areas where dozers cannot be effectively used. They will also focus on mopping up along the fire’s edge and extinguishing any burning or smoldering vegetation. This process may take several days to ensure that there is no threat to the containment lines. Weather and Air Quality: The large high-pressure dome anchored over the Desert Southwest will continue through late week; bringing warm temperatures and low relative humidity. Wildfire smoke from fires across Oregon and southwest Idaho will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. Cooperating Agencies : Juntura RFPA

properties.Location: 25 Miles CW of Jordan Valley, OR
properties.IncidentOverview: Current Situation: On Monday; California Interagency Incident Management Team 5 arrived in Vale; Oregon; to take command of the ongoing Big Grass Fire. We want to take a moment to acknowledge and commend all of the firefighters and the emergency personnel who have been working in challenging conditions to suppress the Big Grass Fire. Yesterday; the fire; which is burning in brush and grass; exhibited extreme behavior with rapid rates of spread; particularly in the afternoon when the winds picked up. Suppression efforts will remain focused on limiting fire growth while protecting threatened communities; residences; livestock; and critical infrastructure. Today; crews will continue to identify and establish effective anchor points to secure containment lines ahead of the advancing fire. The priority areas are in the northeast near Jordan Creek; focusing on reducing the threat to Silver City; and in the southeast near the North Fork of the Owyhee River. Weather and Air Quality: The large high-pressure dome anchored over the Desert Southwest will continue through late week; bringing warm temperatures and low relative humidity. Wildfire smoke from fires across Oregon and southwest Idaho will cause persistent haze and degraded air quality. Area Closure: Access to the North Fork Campground along Juniper Mountain Road in Owyhee County is temporarily closed. This closure is necessary to ensure the safety of both the public and firefighters involved in suppression efforts. Cooperating Agencies: Jordan Valley RFPA; Owyhee RFPA; Malheur County Sheriff’s Office; Owyhee County Sheriff’s Office.
